title: BA1/683/2023 of RAM KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 683 of 2023
Ram Kumar ........Applicant

Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Rajat Mittal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Rakesh Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ashish Naithani, J. (Oral)
1. The applicant is in judicial custody in Case Crime No. 0248 of
2022, under Section 302 IPC, Police Station Selaqui, District
Dehradun. He has sought release on bail.
2. According to the FIR, the applicant and the victim (deceased)
were married. The applicant is alleged to be a drunkard who
often physically assaulted the deceased. On 05.10.2022, the
sister of the deceased (informant) was informed that the victim
was unwell. However, upon reaching the location, she found the
victim dead, leading to the lodging of the FIR.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the
allegations made in the FIR are false and frivolous. The
applicant denies committing any offence and claims he has been
falsely implicated based solely on CCTV footage. According to
the doctor's opinion, the death could have been caused by an
accident, such as an epileptic attack followed by a fall. It is
further alleged that the recovery of the alleged weapon of
offence (the stick) suggests it was planted.
4. On the other hand, the learned State Counsel has argued that, as
per the photographs submitted with the bail application, the
applicant is shown assaulting the victim. According to the
medical report, the victim suffered a head injury inflicted by the
accused using a stick. Furthermore, the autopsy report mentions
a skull fracture, which is identified as a fatal injury.

2
5. During the investigation, the Investigating Officer noted that
CCTV footage shows the accused directly involved in the crime.
The alleged murder weapon (the stick) was also recovered.
6. The CCTV footage, dated 05.10.2022, around 3:00 PM, includes
photographs attached as Annexure No. 4. Specifically, in a
cropped photograph from the footage, a sequence of movements
involving the applicant and the victim is recorded. In Picture
No. 3, the accused appears to be chasing the victim, and in
Picture No. 4, the victim and the accused are seen together,
heading in the opposite direction compared to Pictures Nos. 1, 2,
and 3.
7. In my opinion, without delving into the details as it may affect
the merits of the case, there appear to be sufficient grounds for
bail. Merely viewing the photographs and considering the
medical records submitted does not conclusively establish that
the deceased's death resulted from the alleged brutal assault by
the accused.
8. Having considered the facts and circumstances, this Court finds
that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
9. The bail application is allowed.
10.Let the applicant be released on bail upon executing a personal
bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each in the like
amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
 (Ashish Naithani, J.)
 10.01.2025
R. Uniyal
